source_text: Et hoc peccatum transisse per unum proprie dicitur, si exemplum delinquendi praebuit, inconvenientissime autem, si peccatum istud ingenuit, quod ad posteros nisi per duos transire non potuit.
pass_a_gloss: And this sin is said to have passed through one properly, if he provided an example of doing wrong, but most inconveniently if he generated this sin, which could not pass to posterity except through two.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: And this sin is properly said to have passed through one person if he offered an example of wrongdoing, but most inappropriately if he implanted the sin by generation, since it could not pass to descendants except through two— (Romans 5:12)

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: Repeats or discusses sin entering or passing through one man.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
